title: A Simple and Rapid System for DNA and RNA Isolation from Diverse Plants Using Handmade Kit
author: Farhad Masoomi-Aladizgeh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.2.1347/v2
materials: 10 min Isolation of nucleic acid, Steps 4-

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.5 g CTAB, 1 g EDTA, 2.5 g Tris base and 5 g NaCl in 100 ml autoclaved water while shaking at room temperature; optionally add 10 µl β‑mercaptoethanol per 1 ml buffer for high‑polysaccharide tissues and 15 mg PVPP per 1 ml buffer for high‑polyphenol tissues.

steps.title: Grind tissue in buffer
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.5–1 g of leaf, shoot, root or recalcitrant tissue, add 1 ml of the prepared extraction buffer, and grind thoroughly in a sterilized mortar and pestle (with or without liquid nitrogen) to obtain a homogeneous glaze; perform at room temperature (centrifugation steps later at 4 °C, isopropanol precipitation on ice).

steps.title: Transfer and vortex extract
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenate to a sterile 2 ml centrifuge tube and briefly vortex until fully resuspended.

steps.title: Incubate for cell lysis
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 65 °C for 10 minutes to lyse cells completely.

steps.title: Add chloroform:isoamyl alcohol
steps.instruction: Add 600 µl chloroform : isoamyl alcohol (24 : 1) to each tube and homogenize by vortexing.

steps.title: Centrifuge to separate phases
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13 700 g, 4 °C for 10 minutes; the extraction buffer pH is ~8–9 (adjusting to ~6–7 lowers DNA and raises RNA yields).

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new 1.5 ml tube.

steps.title: Precipitate nucleic acids with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 700 µl cold isopropanol to the transferred phase and invert the tube 3–4 times to mix and precipitate DNA/RNA.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13 700 g, 4 °C for 10 minutes; a white pellet will form at the tube bottom. Do not disturb the lower phases when pipetting the upper liquid.

steps.title: Wash pellet with ethanol
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and gently wash the nucleic‑acid pellet with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Centrifuge and air‑dry pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 5 400 g, 4 °C for 5 minutes, remove the ethanol supernatant and air‑dry the pellet.

steps.title: Dissolve pellet in water
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 20–30 µl RNase‑free (commercial) or autoclaved water.

steps.title: Incubate and store nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Incubate at room temperature for a few minutes, then store the solution at –20 °C for short‑term or –80 °C for long‑term storage.
